newsitem.title: USA: Earthquake rocks remote Aleutian island.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks remote Aleutian island.

text.p: A strong earthquake rocked a remote Aleutian island on Tuesday but there were no reports of damage, officials said.
The federal Tsunami Warning Centre in Palmer, Alaska, said the quake measured 6.6 on the Richter scale and was felt on the island of Adak.
"There was no damage reported, but they felt it," said Tony Tix, a spokesman for the centre.

Although the centre issued a notice of the quake, it judged it too small and too far offshore -- about 365 km (227 miles) southwest of Atka at 51.3 N 179.3 W. -- to warrant a tsunami warning, Tix said. No tide level changes were spotted as a result of the earthquake, he said.

The people living and working on Adak -- about 200 Navy personnel closing down a station there, and a handful of federal biologists -- were jolted by the quake which occurred shortly after 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), Joe Meehan of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service said.
"I thought we were defintely going to get a tsunami warning out of it," Meehan said. "I was in the building here, and it was shaking pretty good."
A few items fell from shelves during the quake, and some people who were lunching at the Navy cafeteria hid under their tables during the shaking, he said.
The island, about 1,200 miles (1920 km) southwest of Anchorage, is the site of a naval station in the stages of shutting down. It is also part of the vast Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge.
Earthquakes are common in the Aleutians, an archipelago of volcanic islands. A quake measuring 7.7 on the Richter scale spurred a tsunami warning last year, but caused no damage.
